title: Béchamel sauce
intro: About 550 ml of smooth, velvety sauce for lasagna, cannelloni and gratins.

steps.t: Heat the milk in a small pan until it almost boils, then turn it off.
In a saucepan, melt the butter over low heat, add all the flour at once and whisk.
Cook the roux for 2 minutes, whisking, until it smells like biscuits but stays pale.
steps.label: Roux

steps.t: Take it off the heat and pour in the hot milk in a thin stream, whisking to avoid lumps.
Return to medium heat and cook for 6 minutes, whisking constantly, until thick enough to coat the spoon.
steps.label: Béchamel

steps.t: Season with salt and nutmeg. If not using right away, press plastic wrap onto the surface.

tips.t: With Bolognese ragù and fresh egg pasta sheets, it's the base of classic lasagna.
For croquettes and firmer fillings, use 70 g of butter and 70 g of flour.
It sets in the fridge: rewarm over low heat with a splash of milk, whisking.

title: Homemade mayonnaise
intro: Ready in a minute with a stick blender: thick, glossy and milder than the jarred kind.

steps.t: Leave the egg at room temperature for 30 minutes. Use very fresh eggs: they stay raw in this sauce.
steps.label: Egg

steps.t: Put the whole egg, mustard, lemon juice and salt in the tall beaker of a stick blender.
Pour all the oil on top and wait a few seconds for the egg to settle at the bottom.
Place the blender on the bottom and blend without moving it for 10 seconds, until a white cream forms below.
Slowly lift it upwards to work in all the oil, until thick and glossy.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon. Keep it in a closed jar in the fridge and eat within 2 days.

tips.t: Add grated garlic for aioli, or chopped capers, gherkins and parsley for tartar sauce.
If it splits, put a fresh yolk in a bowl and whisk the split sauce into it in a thin stream.

title: Piedmont green sauce
intro: Bagnet verd: parsley, anchovies and capers chopped by hand, made for boiled meats.

steps.t: Cook the egg in boiling water for 9 minutes, cool it in cold water, peel it and keep the yolk.
steps.label: Egg

steps.t: Meanwhile, soak the bread in the vinegar for 5 minutes to soften, then squeeze it well.
steps.label: Bread

steps.t: Finely chop the parsley with a knife, together with the garlic, capers and anchovies.
Add the bread and the crumbled yolk and keep chopping until everything is fine and even.
Transfer to a bowl and stir in the oil in a thin stream, until thick.
Let it rest for 30 minutes at room temperature so the flavors come together.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: It's the sauce for bollito misto, and great on the poached chicken from the stock or on boiled eggs.
Covered with oil in a jar, it keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Classic vinaigrette
intro: Mustard, vinegar and shallot whisked with oil: the French dressing for salads.

steps.t: Mince the shallot very finely and leave it in the vinegar with the salt for 10 minutes to mellow its bite.
steps.label: Shallot

steps.t: Add the mustard and whisk until the salt dissolves.
Drizzle in the oil while whisking constantly, until the dressing is emulsified and slightly thick.
Add pepper and taste it on a lettuce leaf: adjust the acidity and salt.
Dress the salad just before serving. In a closed jar it keeps 5 days in the fridge: shake before using.

tips.t: Perfect on butter lettuce and endive, boiled leeks, warm lentils or potatoes.
Put everything in a closed jar and shake hard for 20 seconds: perfect emulsion, no whisk.
Swap the vinegar for lemon juice and add a teaspoon of honey for a softer version.

title: Tahini sauce
intro: Sesame paste, lemon and garlic whipped with ice water: pale, silky and bright.

steps.t: Grate the garlic very finely and leave it in the lemon juice with the salt for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Strain the juice for a milder taste, add the tahini and stir: it seizes and looks split, that's normal.
Add the ice water a spoonful at a time, whisking, until pale, smooth and creamy.
Season with the cumin, taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
It thickens in the fridge: loosen it with a splash of water before serving.

tips.t: Serve with falafel, roasted cauliflower, shawarma or grilled fish.
Blend it with a bunch of parsley for the green version, tahini khadra.

title: Teriyaki sauce
intro: Soy, mirin, sake and sugar reduced to a glossy glaze: sweet, salty and deep.

steps.t: In a small pan, bring the sake and mirin to a boil and let them bubble for 1 minute to cook off the alcohol.
steps.label: Alcohol

steps.t: Add the soy sauce and sugar and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 9 minutes, until reduced by a third and it coats the spoon.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: For a thicker glaze, stir in the cornstarch mixed with the cold water and cook for 1 minute, stirring.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Let it cool: it thickens further. Kept in a closed jar in the fridge, it lasts 2 weeks.

tips.t: Brush it on salmon, chicken thighs or tofu in the last 2-3 minutes of cooking.
Use tamari instead of soy sauce to make it gluten-free.
Add grated fresh ginger and a crushed garlic clove while it reduces.

title: Chimichurri
intro: Parsley, garlic, oregano and vinegar: the Argentine sauce made for the asado.

steps.t: Dissolve the salt in the hot water: this salmuera is what seasons the sauce.
Finely chop the parsley and garlic with a knife; a blender would turn them to mush.
In a jar, mix the parsley, garlic, oregano and pepper flakes.
Add the vinegar and salted water, then the oil, and stir well.
Let it rest for at least 1 hour at room temperature so the flavors meld.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve at room temperature, stirring first. Covered with oil in the fridge, it keeps a week.

tips.t: Spoon it over asado, grilled steak, choripán or grilled vegetables.
For red chimichurri, add a teaspoon of sweet paprika and half a red bell pepper, finely chopped.
